notes: Snapshot of 11 November 2026. US state law follows the IIHS table, with service status from robotaxi trackers; most non-US records rest on secondary trackers, law-firm notes and press, not regulators. Tesla "unsupervised" means the Tesla Robotaxi fleet in Texas and Florida only; no customer-owned car runs unsupervised.

ARE.summary: WeRide and Uber run fully driverless paid rides in Abu Dhabi and Dubai; a federal self-driving law was approved in 2026.

AUS.summary: The national Automated Vehicle Safety Law is not yet in force and is targeted for 2027; Tesla FSD Supervised is on sale.

AUT.summary: Austria has made no national decision on Tesla FSD and is waiting for an EU-wide vote.

BEL.summary: Tesla FSD Supervised was approved in June 2026; the Leuven autonomous shuttle still carries a safety officer.

BRA.summary: Brazil has no autonomous vehicle law; Bill 1317/2023 is still pending in Congress.

CAN.summary: Rules are provincial: Ontario runs a testing pilot to 2027 and British Columbia bans Level 3 and above; Waymo plans Toronto for 2028.

CHE.summary: A March 2025 ordinance allows driverless vehicles on approved routes under remote supervision; services are still in testing.

CHN.summary: Driverless robotaxis from Baidu, Pony.ai and WeRide carry the public in Wuhan, Beijing, Guangzhou and Shenzhen under city permits.

CZE.summary: Czechia recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in September 2026 for driver-supervised use.

DEU.summary: A 2021 law allows Level 4 driverless operation in approved areas with a permit, but no regular service runs yet; FSD awaits an EU decision.

DNK.summary: Denmark recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in June 2026 and it is rolling out to customers.

ESP.summary: A national road-testing framework has applied since 2025; WeRide runs in Madrid with operators on board and Waymo plans riders in 2027.

EST.summary: A fixed-route shuttle at Tallinn airport runs with no operator on board; Estonia recognised Tesla FSD Supervised in May 2026.

FIN.summary: Finland recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised on 10 November 2026; rollout to customers was about to begin.

FRA.summary: Driverless vehicles may run only as automated road transport systems on set routes under a 2021 decree; Level 3 is allowed.

GBR.summary: Driverless passenger service permits opened in May 2026 under the Automated Vehicles Act 2024, but none is in use; Wayve rides in London have a safety driver.

HKG.summary: Pilot licences only, with a trained backup operator required; Baidu Apollo Go is testing with no public riders.

HRV.summary: Verne runs paid robotaxi rides in Zagreb with an operator on board, and driverless rides for invited passengers began in September 2026.

HUN.summary: Hungary has made no national decision on Tesla FSD and is following EU developments.

IDN.summary: Indonesia has no autonomous vehicle legislation and relies on existing traffic law.

IND.summary: India has no autonomous vehicle law and its transport minister has said driverless cars will not be allowed.

IRL.summary: No approval for Tesla FSD Supervised yet; Tesla is in talks with Irish regulators.

ISR.summary: Supervised trials only; the transport ministry expects rules for Level 4 robotaxis to take effect in the second half of 2027.

ITA.summary: Rules cover supervised road testing only; Italy has not recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD and backs an EU-wide decision.

JPN.summary: Level 4 driverless operation has been legal by prefectural permit since April 2023; Waymo plans public rides in Tokyo in 2027.

KAZ.summary: Rules issued in mid-2026 set a three-year pilot that allows driverless taxis in Astana, Almaty and Kosshy; service is planned for 2027.

KOR.summary: Paid autonomous rides are allowed only in designated pilot zones, and Seoul robotaxis still carry a safety supervisor.

LTU.summary: Lithuania recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in May 2026 and it is rolling out to customers.

LUX.summary: Luxembourg has authorised supervised testing only, including a 12-month Level 4 pilot with Pony.ai.

LVA.summary: Latvia recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in October 2026; rollout to customers was still pending.

MEX.summary: Mexico has no legal framework for autonomous driving and no federal bill; Tesla sells FSD Supervised there.

MYS.summary: Malaysia allows testing under transport ministry guidelines, with a public test route in Cyberjaya; its roadmap targets Level 3 by 2030.

NLD.summary: Driverless road experiments are allowed by permit, and the RDW approved Tesla FSD Supervised in April 2026, a first in Europe.

NOR.summary: A 2017 testing law governs trials; the Oslo pilot carries an operator on board, and Norway will follow the EU decision on Tesla FSD.

NZL.summary: There is no dedicated autonomous vehicle law, though existing law does not require a driver to be present; Tesla FSD Supervised is on sale.

POL.summary: Poland requires local testing before any approval of Tesla FSD Supervised.

PRT.summary: Portugal has not recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised.

QAT.summary: Pony.ai and Mowasalat run a public robotaxi service in Doha with a safety operator on board; driverless rides are invitation-only tests.

ROU.summary: Romania has not recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD; its road code bars drivers from releasing the steering wheel.

RUS.summary: Robotaxis run under experimental regimes with a safety driver; a draft law to remove the driver would take effect in September 2027.

SAU.summary: WeRide robotaxis run on Uber in Riyadh with operators on board under a transport authority trial.

SGP.summary: Grab and WeRide carry the public on approved routes in Punggol with a safety operator on board; Waymo plans driverless service in 2028.

SVK.summary: Slovakia recognised the Dutch approval of Tesla FSD Supervised in October 2026 for driver-supervised use.

SVN.summary: Slovenia approved Tesla FSD Supervised in September 2026 for driver-supervised use.

SWE.summary: Only limited tests with trained drivers are permitted; Tesla FSD has public road testing approval but customers cannot use it.

THA.summary: Thailand has no autonomous vehicle law; general traffic and vehicle law applies.

TUR.summary: A December 2024 regulation sets EU-style type approval for automated driving systems; no driverless service operates.

TWN.summary: Autonomous vehicles run only as time-limited sandbox trials under the 2019 unmanned vehicles experimentation act.

US-AK.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-AL.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver on board; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-AR.summary: Driverless operation is allowed under a state-approved program, with a licensed driver on board for the first six months.

US-AZ.summary: Waymo runs public driverless rides across metro Phoenix; state law lets Level 4 and 5 vehicles operate with no licensed driver.

US-CA.summary: Waymo carries the public driverless in the Bay Area, Los Angeles and San Diego under DMV and CPUC permits; Tesla still uses safety drivers.

US-CO.summary: Waymo driverless rides began in Denver in September 2026, by invitation at first; state law allows Level 4 and 5 deployment.

US-CT.summary: Testing pilot only under state statute, with a human operator required.

US-DC.summary: Testing only: a test operator must be in the vehicle at first, and paid service is not authorized; a robotaxi bill is before the Council.

US-DE.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-FL.summary: Waymo and Tesla Robotaxi both run driverless public rides in Miami, Orlando and Tampa; state law needs no permit or human driver.

US-GA.summary: Waymo driverless rides run in Atlanta through the Uber app; state law lets Level 4 and 5 vehicles operate with no licensed driver.

US-HI.summary: Testing only under a 2020 pilot law; Level 4 and 5 vehicles need a licensed driver on board.

US-IA.summary: State law allows deployment of automated driving system vehicles with no licensed driver on board; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-ID.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-IL.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; Waymo has named Chicago as a future city but nothing operates yet.

US-IN.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-KS.summary: State law allows driverless deployment, with a licensed driver on board for the first 12 months in most passenger vehicles.

US-KY.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver on board once a law enforcement plan is filed; no public service yet.

US-LA.summary: State law allows driverless commercial trucks only; other vehicles are not addressed. Waymo lists New Orleans as a future city.

US-MA.summary: Testing only under MassDOT agreements, with a licensed test driver in the vehicle; no AV statute.

US-MD.summary: Testing is allowed with a licensed driver in the vehicle; there is no deployment law. Waymo lists Baltimore as a future city.

US-ME.summary: State pilot rules cover testing only and do not require a licensed driver in the vehicle; no deployment law.

US-MI.summary: State law allows driverless testing and manufacturer-run on-demand networks; Waymo plans Detroit but no public service runs yet.

US-MN.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; May Mobility shuttles run with an operator on board and Waymo has announced Minneapolis.

US-MO.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-MS.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-MT.summary: A 2025 law allows Level 4 and 5 deployment subject to state rulemaking; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-NC.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; Waymo has named Charlotte as a future city but no service runs yet.

US-ND.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-NE.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles to operate with no operator present in the vehicle; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-NH.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver on board, subject to conditions; no public service yet.

US-NJ.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-NM.summary: Fully autonomous vehicles may run with nobody on board after a filing with the state transport department; no public service yet.

US-NV.summary: Zoox carries the public driverless on the Las Vegas Strip and Waymo rides are by invitation; paid service needs a state permit.

US-NY.summary: Testing pilot only, extended to April 2028; a licensed driver must be in the vehicle and there is no path to driverless service.

US-OH.summary: State rules cover testing only but allow it with no licensed driver in the vehicle; no deployment law or public service.

US-OK.summary: State law allows Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver given a law enforcement plan and $1 million cover; no service yet.

US-OR.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law beyond naming ODOT as lead agency; Waymo has named Portland as a future city.

US-PA.summary: Highly automated vehicles may run with no driver under a PennDOT certificate; Waymo has announced Philadelphia and Pittsburgh.

US-RI.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-SC.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-SD.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-TN.summary: Waymo opened driverless rides to everyone in Nashville in June 2026; state law lets Level 4 and 5 vehicles run with no licensed driver.

US-TX.summary: Waymo and Tesla run driverless rides in Austin, Dallas, Houston and San Antonio; commercial driverless service needs TxDMV authorization.

US-UT.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-VA.summary: No general AV statute: the only law covers driverless work-zone crash trucks. A licensing bill was carried over to 2027.

US-VT.summary: Testing only; vehicles need a licensed driver on board and deployment is not addressed.

US-WA.summary: State law covers testing only and allows it with no human operator on board; commercial driverless service is not addressed.

US-WI.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

US-WV.summary: State law allows deployment of Level 4 and 5 vehicles with no licensed driver; no public robotaxi service yet.

US-WY.summary: No state autonomous vehicle law; driverless operation is not addressed.

USA.summary: Law is set state by state: driverless robotaxis carry the public in eight states, while others allow testing only or have no AV law.

ZAF.summary: South Africa has no legislation for autonomous vehicles, which cannot use public roads until rules exist.
